statement: A* returns a least-cost path whenever the heuristic h is non-negative and satisfies h(goal) = 0, even if h overestimates the remaining cost at some states.
definitions: A*: best-first search over the open list ordered by f(v) = g(v) + h(v) where g is the cost of the path found so far; the search stops and returns the path when a goal node is popped (expanded), not when it is generated. Either tree-search or graph-search (closed set) may be assumed; the counterexample must fail under the chosen convention. Edge costs positive, h non-negative, h(goal) = 0.
ground_truth_witness: Directed graph S->A (cost 1), A->G (cost 1), S->B (cost 1), B->G (cost 5), with heuristic h(S) = 0, h(A) = 100, h(B) = 0, h(G) = 0. h is non-negative and h(G) = 0, but it is inadmissible at A, where the true cost-to-go is 1. A* expands S, then compares f(A) = 1 + 100 = 101 with f(B) = 1 + 0 = 1, expands B, then reaches G with g = 6 and f = 6 < 101, so it returns the path S->B->G of cost 6. The optimal path is S->A->G of cost 2.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: False and the witness is valid: simulated A* in both tree-search and graph-search form, it expands S then B then G and returns S->B->G of cost 6 while S->A->G costs 2. Ambiguity only in what 'A*' is (goal test at pop time, tree vs graph search, tie-breaking) - the witness is robust to all of these, so pin the convention and admit. Roster has no heuristic-search item.
